subject.title: fix(cli): drop in-flight code-server upstream opened after bridge Close

question: Should this PR require a live coordinator-and-lease `crabbox code` shutdown proof, or should maintainers explicitly override the proof gate because the deterministic test forces the exact race over real local WebSocket connections?
rationale: The implementation and regression are convincing at source level, but repository review policy treats tests and `httptest` environments as supplemental rather than after-fix real behavior proof for an external PR.

options.title: Require live bridge proof
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until a maintainer or contributor posts redacted runtime logs or terminal evidence from a real coordinator-backed code-server session.

options.title: Approve a proof override
options.body: Explicitly accept the deterministic real-WebSocket regression as sufficient for this difficult-to-stage shutdown race.

recommendation.title: Require live bridge proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR blocked until a maintainer or contributor posts redacted runtime logs or terminal evidence from a real coordinator-backed code-server session.

likelyOwner.reason: They requested review and controlled autosquash on this PR, so they are the clearest available owner for the proof-gate decision.
